narrative.northStar: The Item Tooltip of Where You Stand
narrative.overview:
Every surface Exile Companion draws is a Path of Exile item tooltip. The zone is the item name in a tinted header band, the things to do there are its properties, and the way out is the last line, "Then:". The overlay, the quick menu and each settings group use the same parts: a see-through black body with no frame, a header band with rules along both edges and wedge ends that meet in a diamond, short glowing separators, centered small caps, and text colours that mean what they mean in the game.

The system is dense and quiet. It is read in glances over a busy, dark game scene, so it has no fills, gradients or accents beyond what the game's own tooltips carry, and colour is spent only on meaning: a boss name is red because the game's corrupted red is the danger colour, a waypoint is blue because it is magic. The overlay window is transparent and fitted to its content; only the plate paints. The settings window is an ordinary window, but its groups are still tooltips standing on a dark ground.

It rejects the web-app card (rounded corners, drop shadows, coloured buttons) and the generic brown-and-gold fantasy panel. The chrome is neutral grey and black; the only warm hue in the frame is the sand tint for towns.
keyCharacteristics: See-through black bodies, opacity set by the player (50 to 100 percent on the overlay).
A header band per tooltip, tinted by kind, with 1px rules along its top and bottom edges and, at each end, a wedge drawn from both corners to a 7px diamond on the middle.
Alegreya Sans SC at medium weight for all tooltip text; Alegreya Sans italic for flavour.

rules.name: The Game's Meaning Rule
rules.body: A hue appears only where the game uses it for the same meaning. New content picks the matching item text colour; if the game has none for that meaning, it stays grey or white.

rules.name: The Grey Ladder Rule
rules.body: Brightness is rank: Label Grey for what something is, Plain Grey for running text, Normal Item White for chrome, Value White for what the player acts on.

rules.name: The Tint by Kind Rule
rules.body: One tint per tooltip drives its band, rules, corners and separators together. Areas and app chrome use Normal Item White, towns use Currency Sand.

rules.name: The Small Caps Voice Rule
rules.body: Everything in a tooltip is Alegreya Sans SC at 500. Switch to Alegreya Sans for flavour (italic) and for literal strings: key names, file paths, speed multipliers.

rules.name: The Size as Rank Rule
rules.body: The current actions are the largest body text (15px) and the brightest; the properties line and labels drop to 13px grey; key hints sit at 11px. Do not add a size between these steps.

rules.name: The No Frame Rule
rules.body: A tooltip body has no border and no shadow. The only frame is the pair of 1px tint rules inside the header band, 2px from its top and bottom and stopping 40px short of each end. The one exception is state: an unlocked overlay gets a 1px white outline at 35 percent, 2px out, while it can be dragged.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded. Ornament lives only in the header corners.

dos: Do build every new panel as a tooltip: a header band tinted by kind over a see-through black body with no frame.

Do colour route content only with the game's item text colours, by meaning (Magic Blue for waypoints and portals, Corrupted Red for bosses, Quest Green for quests, Unique Brown for trials and arenas, Gem Teal for gems).
Do keep the overlay's bottom center fixed and let new content grow upward.
Do set tooltip text in Alegreya Sans SC 500 and switch to Alegreya Sans for flavour, key names and paths.
Do draw small marks as inline SVG in currentColor.
Do show state on buttons with the pressed treatment (Normal Item White border, Value White text), not with a fill colour.
donts: Don't round corners or add drop shadows; the system is square and flat.
Don't put a border around a tooltip body; the frame belongs to the header band.
Don't bring back the brown-and-gold fantasy chrome; the frame is neutral grey and black.
Don't use a route colour for decoration or for chrome.
Don't add a type size between the existing steps (11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 19px).
Don't use the game's header art or GGG logos; the header frame and diamonds are Exile Companion's own.
